title: Cheese Quesadillas
subtitle: Flour tortillas filled with melted cheese and crispy in a pan
excerpt: Flour tortillas filled with grated Cheddar and spring onion, folded and cooked in a dry pan until the outside is golden and crisp and the cheese inside has melted. Ready in under 10 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Quesadillas are a Mexican street food and home staple, consisting of a corn or flour tortilla filled with cheese and cooked on a griddle or comal until the cheese melts. The British version typically uses flour tortillas and Cheddar in place of the traditional queso Oaxaca or Chihuahua. Any filling that melts or heats through quickly works: cooked chicken, black beans, and roasted peppers are all popular additions.

content.text: Cook in a dry pan over medium heat: no oil is needed and added fat makes the tortilla greasy rather than crisp. Fold the tortilla in half over the filling to make a half-moon. Flip once the underside is golden. The quesadilla is done when both sides are golden and the cheese inside is completely melted.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Place one tortilla in the pan. Scatter half the cheese and half the spring onion over one half of the tortilla. Add chilli flakes if using.
Fold the empty half of the tortilla over the filling to make a half-moon shape. Press down with a spatula. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is golden and the cheese begins to melt.

Flip carefully with a spatula. Cook for a further 2 minutes until the second side is golden. Slide onto a board and cut into wedges. Repeat with the remaining tortilla. Serve with soured cream and salsa.
